raw_comment:
I noticed that surprisingly, California did not have as much of an extreme drought area as I would have thought. I often heard about wildfires due to such dry conditions and expected more. I was also surprised to notice that there were dark colors (severe drought) in the northeast which I would not have expected. I also noticed that Texas has many different levels throughout the state depending on the area. 

I wonder what the cause of the drought in Ohio/West Virginia is because their weather is not super hot or dry usually, so it seems a little unusual for their climate to be so dry. 

This relates to me and my community because even though the specific area of Michigan where we are located is a lightly colored section, there are other darker-colored parts of Michigan surrounding us. This might have an effect on growing crops like corn. I see many cornfields around my town and I know that a drought may affect them which could affect the prices of crops or supply.

America is drying up, watery going to do about it?
